# Katahdin (01, engineer) — BAD-085

## Brief
Make the Server integration skip gate in .github/workflows/server-ci.yml actually
print the skip reasons it promises.

The bug: the step's failure branch runs `grep -oE "skip: .*" /tmp/server-tests.log`.
No node test reporter ever emits the string `skip: `. The gate therefore fails the
job on any skip and then prints `Reasons:` followed by nothing. The count grep
(`skipped [0-9]+`) is correct and must keep working untouched.

What to work out for yourself, with evidence, before writing the fix:

1. Which reporter the step actually gets. The command is
   `node --test "test/server/**/*.test.mjs" 2>&1 | tee /tmp/server-tests.log`.
   node's default reporter depends on whether stdout is a TTY — in CI it is a
   pipe. Determine what that means here (this repo runs Node 22.14; check what
   the runner uses too) and confirm it by running a real command whose stdout is
   a pipe, not by reasoning about it. Capture the exact bytes a skipped test
   produces in that mode.
2. Whether the fix should cover only that reporter or both spec and tap. A grep
   that matches both is fine if it does not also match unrelated lines (a
   comment, a diagnostic, a test name containing `# `); a grep that matches both
   badly is worse than one that matches the real reporter exactly. Decide, and
   say why in the commit message.
3. That the reasons it prints are readable. BAD-084 gave these skips real,
   distinct reasons (half-up stack vs absent stack vs no container runtime, each
   naming a different repair). `sort -u` over them should give the operator one
   line per distinct cause, with the reason text intact — not a wall of per-test
   duplicates and not a truncated fragment.

Verification, and this is the part that matters: you cannot run the CI job, so
prove it locally against real reporter output. Produce a log the same way the
step does (a real `node --test` run over a file in `test/server/` that skips —
with no local Supabase stack up, the suite skips cleanly by design, which is
exactly the input the gate sees) and run the *new* grep pipeline over that log.
Show the before (empty) and after (reasons) output in your Result. Also check
the count grep still reads the right number off the same log. If you cannot get
a skipping log that way, synthesize one from genuine reporter bytes and say so.
Do not claim it works from reading the YAML.

Also update the step's comment block. It currently explains the earlier bug
(grepping for ONE reason); it should also record this one — that the reason
string it matched never existed — so the next person does not reintroduce either.
Keep the existing comment's voice and do not pad it.

Scope: this one workflow step. Do not touch the suite, the stack setup steps, or
any other workflow. If you find something else wrong, `proposal file` it.

## Log
- 2026-09-16T10:40 Evidence: node 22.23.2 (matches CI's .nvmrc '22') with stdout piped emits TAP: a skip is 'ok N - <name> # SKIP <reason>'. Node 26 piped emits spec: '- <name> (Xms) # <reason>'. So CI today gets TAP and the step's 'skip: ' grep matches nothing. Count grep reads '# skipped N' in both.
- 2026-09-16T10:46 Decision: match tap exactly AND pin --test-reporter=tap on the command. A both-reporter grep would have to anchor spec on either the multi-byte skip glyph (which this step's own comment forbids) or a bare '# ', which tap fills with '# Subtest:' / '# tests N' / '# skipped N' — the 'matches both badly' case. Pinning removes the question: node 26 with the pin emits byte-identical tap, so a .nvmrc bump cannot silently re-break it. Extraction: sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*ok [0-9]+ - .* # SKIP (.+)$/\1/p' | sort -u. The space before '#' matters: tap escapes a hash inside a test NAME as '\#', so requiring ' # SKIP ' drops the false positive a bare '# SKIP .*' grep produces (proved on a test named 'a name with # SKIP inside it').

## Result
Fixed the Server integration skip gate in .github/workflows/server-ci.yml (one step, 32 added / 7 removed). Uncommitted on fix/bad-085-skip-reasons.

REPORTER EVIDENCE (run, not reasoned). CI's setup-node reads .nvmrc ('22') so it gets the latest 22.x; node 22.23.2 with stdout piped emits TAP, where a skip is the line 'ok N - <name> # SKIP <reason>'. Node 26 piped emits spec instead ('glyph <name> (Xms) # <reason>'), so the non-TTY default HAS moved between those versions. Neither emits 'skip: ' — that string is how the reason reads in the test SOURCE, test(name, { skip: '...' }), which is evidently where the old grep came from.

THE FIX. (a) pinned --test-reporter=tap on the run command; (b) replaced the grep with a sed -nE extraction anchored on 'ok <digits> - ' ... ' # SKIP ' capturing the rest of the line, piped to sort -u, assigned to a reasons variable, with a loud fallback that dumps raw skip lines if nothing parses. The skip-count grep is untouched.

WHY TAP-ONLY PLUS THE PIN, not a both-reporter grep: spec's only anchors are its multi-byte skip glyph — which this step's own comment forbids anchoring on — or a bare hash-space, which TAP fills with '# Subtest:', '# tests N' and '# skipped N'. That is exactly the 'matches both badly' case. Pinning makes the question moot: node 26 WITH the pin emits byte-identical TAP and still prints '# skipped 3', so a .nvmrc bump cannot silently re-break this. The space before the hash in the pattern is load-bearing: TAP escapes a hash inside a test NAME as backslash-hash, so requiring ' # SKIP ' drops a false positive that a bare '# SKIP .*' grep produces — proved against a test literally named 'a name with # SKIP inside it', which the naive grep reported as a reason reading 'inside it'.

VERIFIED. Extracted the step's run block verbatim out of the YAML (python yaml.safe_load) and ran it under 'bash -e' (Actions' default shell) from the repo root, node 22.23.2 on PATH, SUPABASE_URL at a dead port so the suite skips exactly as it does with no stack. Real log: 553 tests, 121 skipped, 0 fail.
  BEFORE: the old 'skip: ' grep over that log -> zero lines.
  AFTER:  'reported skips: 121', then one line — 'local Supabase not running - see server/README.md section Local development (podman: DOCKER_HOST + -x edge-runtime,vector,logflare), or let the Server integration CI check run it' — then exit 1.
  COUNT:  the unchanged count grep still reads 121 off that same log, matching its '# skipped 121' summary line.
Distinctness: concatenated that log with a second real run pointed at a 503 stand-in (the half-up-stack condition). 124 genuine TAP skip lines in, exactly 2 lines out, one per cause, reason text intact — em dash, section sign, backticked repair command, all of it. The harness says openly that this is two runs concatenated, because one stack state can only ever produce one of those reasons.
actionlint: my step is clean; the two pre-existing SC2012/SC2010 findings are in the migration-count and serve steps, which I did not touch. Nothing in CI lints workflows, and actionlint would not have caught this bug anyway (a grep that matches nothing is valid shell).

COMMENT BLOCK. Records both bugs in the existing voice. The first (grepping for ONE reason) is kept verbatim; added that its replacement matched a source string that no reporter's output contains, so the gate failed the job on every skip and printed 'Reasons:' followed by nothing — the same silence, produced by the fix for it — plus why the reporter is now pinned.

PROPOSED COMMIT MESSAGE BODY: 'node --test picks its reporter from whether stdout is a TTY, and under a pipe it is not. On Node 22 that means tap, where a skip reads ok N - <name> # SKIP <reason>. The step grepped for skip: , which is the shape of the reason in the test source and of no reporter output, so every skip failed the job and printed an empty reason list. Match tap, and pin it. Covering spec as well would mean anchoring on its multi-byte skip glyph, which this step already says never to do, or on a bare hash that tap fills with # Subtest: and # tests N — worse than matching the real reporter exactly. Pinning is the cheaper answer and it also holds when .nvmrc moves past the Node where the non-TTY default became spec.'
